title: Studio apartment
description: One room for sleeping, cooking and everything else.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Come on in! Sorry, it's a bit small.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Small but cozy. I love how much light you get through the blinds.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Thanks. Make yourself at home. You can sit on the bed.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Wow, you've got a rice cooker and an induction cooktop. That's a whole kitchen.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Pretty much. The mini fridge is the only thing that's really too small.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Well, it's perfect for one person. Honestly, I'm a little jealous.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Is it just me, or is it really hot tonight?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It's not just you. Can we turn on the air conditioner?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Sure. The remote is next to the desk lamp.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Got it. Should I close the blinds too?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes, please. And could you plug my phone into the power strip?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Done. Now let's hope we can actually get some sleep.

selfTalk.text: The air conditioner above the counter makes a humming noise that I only notice when I'm trying to sleep.
I'm going to clean the air conditioner filter this weekend, because it's starting to smell dusty.
If my electricity bill is this high again, I'll have to use the air conditioner a lot less.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: It's so hot in here. Do you mind if I turn on the air conditioner?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Go ahead. The remote's on the bed.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Thanks. Is seventy-five degrees okay for you?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Perfect. Just set the timer so it doesn't run all night.

selfTalk.text: The blinds in my apartment are half-open, so thin stripes of sunlight fall across the floor.
Before I start work, I'll pull up the blinds and let some natural light into the room.
I feel a bit exposed when the blinds are open at night, because the neighbors can see right in.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: It's really bright in here this afternoon.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Do you want me to close the blinds a little?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Yes, please. I can't see my laptop screen at all.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: There you go. If you tilt them like this, you still get some light.

selfTalk.text: My wardrobe is so full of clothes that the doors won't close properly anymore.
I'm going to clear out my wardrobe and give away everything I haven't worn in a year.
Every time I open the wardrobe, I feel like I have nothing to wear, even though it's packed.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Can I hang my coat somewhere?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sure, there's space in the wardrobe, I think.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Are you sure? It looks like it's about to burst.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Okay, maybe just put it on the back of the door. I really need to sort it out.

selfTalk.text: The door lock on my apartment has a keypad, so I don't have to carry my keys around anymore.
I'll change the code on the door lock, because I gave the old one to the plumber.
Even when I know I've locked the door, I sometimes go back just to check the door lock again.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Hey, your door lock keeps beeping. Is the battery dying?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Probably. It's been doing that for a few days.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: You should replace it soon. What if it stops working while you're out?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Good point. I'd be locked out of my own apartment.

selfTalk.text: My mini fridge is so small that a carton of milk and some leftovers take up all the space.
I'm going to clean out the mini fridge tonight, because something in there smells terrible.
I'd love a bigger fridge, but there's no space for one in a studio this tiny.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Is there anything to drink in your mini fridge?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: There should be some sparkling water on the bottom shelf.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Found it. Wow, you really don't keep much food in here.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I know. I buy groceries every couple of days because it fills up so quickly.

selfTalk.text: The rice cooker sitting on top of the fridge is the only kitchen appliance I use every day.
Before I leave for work, I'll rinse the rice and set the rice cooker so dinner is ready when I get home.
I can't imagine living without my rice cooker, since it makes perfect rice without any effort.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Something smells good. Is that the rice cooker?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Yes, I put some rice on about half an hour ago.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Do you ever cook anything other than rice in it?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sometimes I make soup or steam vegetables. It's surprisingly useful.

selfTalk.text: The induction cooktop on my counter is just one flat black panel, but it boils water incredibly fast.
I'll wipe down the induction cooktop after dinner so the stains don't burn on tomorrow.
I was nervous about using an induction cooktop at first, but now I prefer it to a gas stove.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: How do I turn on this cooktop? There are no knobs.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Just touch the power button and then press plus to turn up the heat.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Oh, it's already hot. That was quick.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Be careful, though. It only works with certain pans, so use the black one.

selfTalk.text: The drying rack by the window is covered with socks and towels that still feel a bit damp.
I'll fold up the drying rack before my friends come over, so the room doesn't look so messy.
I'd rather use a drying rack than a dryer, because my clothes last longer that way.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Sorry, can I move your drying rack? I need to get to the window.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Of course. Just be careful, the shirts on top are still wet.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Don't your clothes take forever to dry in here?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Not in summer. In winter, though, I sometimes have to wait two days.

selfTalk.text: The desk lamp on my nightstand has a bendable arm, so I can point the light right at my book.
I'm going to switch off the desk lamp and finally get some sleep before midnight.
I love reading in bed with just the desk lamp on, because the whole room feels warm and quiet.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Is my lamp too bright for you? I'm trying to finish this chapter.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: It's okay, but could you angle it away from my side a bit?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Sure. How's that?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Much better, thanks. Don't stay up too late, though.

selfTalk.text: My bed takes up almost half of the apartment, so it's also where I eat, read and work.
I'm going to make my bed as soon as I get up, because it makes the whole room look tidier.
On cold mornings, getting out of bed is honestly the hardest part of my whole day.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Where should I sit? There's only one chair.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Just sit on the bed. Everyone does.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: It's really comfortable. No wonder you never want to get up.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I know. That's why I set three alarms every morning.

selfTalk.text: The laundry basket in front of my wardrobe is overflowing, so I definitely need to do laundry tonight.
I'll carry the laundry basket down to the washing machine before anyone else takes it.
I always feel a bit embarrassed when guests see my laundry basket piled high with dirty clothes.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Do you want me to move this laundry basket off the floor?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Oh, sorry! I was going to do the laundry this morning, but I ran out of time.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: No problem. Is there a laundry room in the building?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Yes, in the basement, but there's always a line on weekends.

selfTalk.text: Every socket on my power strip is taken by a charger, so there's no room left for my laptop.
I'll switch off the power strip before I leave, so nothing is wasting electricity all day.
I get a little worried when I see how many cables are plugged into one cheap power strip.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Is there anywhere I can charge my phone?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: There's a power strip on the floor by the rack. You might have to unplug something.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Can I unplug this one? I'm not sure what it's for.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: That's the lamp, so go ahead. I'll plug it back in later.
